name: Ma Long
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest world champion in table tennis history at age 17, winning gold at the 2006 Bremen World Team Championship.
early_history_summary: Ma Long started playing table tennis at age 5 in Anshan, China, encouraged by his father for fitness. He joined the Liaoning Provincial Sports School at 11, was scouted by Beijing at 13, and made the Chinese National B Team at 14. He won four titles at the 2004 World Junior Championships before becoming the youngest world champion at 17 in 2006.
family_context_summary: Born to Ma Yajun and his wife in Anshan, a steel city in Liaoning Province. His father, a non-table-tennis player, insisted Ma Long take up the sport at age 5 for fitness. His mother later quit her job to accompany him when he left Anshan at age 11.
parent_family_domain_summary: Neither parent played table tennis; they provided emotional and logistical support but no domain expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chinese national table tennis system, early specialization, provincial sports school, dedicated coaches
evidence_summary: Ma Long's path to becoming the youngest world champion at 17 was built on China's elite table tennis pipeline: starting at 5, entering provincial sports school at 11, being scouted by Beijing at 13, and joining the national team at 14. His parents were not table tennis players but supported him logistically, with his mother quitting her job to accompany him. Multiple dedicated coaches from childhood provided sustained individualized training. By 17, he had accumulated over 12 years of intense practice within the world's most competitive table tennis system.
starting_point: Born to a middle-class family in Anshan, Liaoning Province; father Ma Yajun was a non-table-tennis professional who encouraged the sport for fitness, mother was a homemaker who later quit her job to support his training.
current_position: Widely considered the greatest table tennis player of all time; six-time Olympic gold medalist (2012-2024); withdrew from ITTF world rankings in December 2024; elected vice president of the Chinese Table Tennis Association in April 2025.

name: Dominik Hašek
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest professional hockey player in Czechoslovak history at age 16, joining HC Pardubice in the Czechoslovak Extraliga in 1980; by age 25 he had won two league titles and been named the league's best player three times (1987, 1989, 1990).
early_history_summary: Hašek started playing hockey at age 6 in Pardubice, Czechoslovakia, initially as a goalie for a 9-year-old team. He joined HC Pardubice in the top Czechoslovak league at 16, becoming the youngest professional player in history. He won the Extraliga's Goaltender of the Year award from 1986-1990 and was named league MVP in 1987, 1989, and 1990.
family_context_summary: Born Dominik Kaštánek to Alois and Marie in Pardubice; parents divorced when he was 2, and his mother remarried Jan Hašek who adopted him. His father/stepfather bought him his first goalie pads at age 6 and fashioned a blocker from rubber and a regular glove.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was a miner and hockey fan who took him to tryouts and supported his early hockey involvement; his grandfather also took him to local hockey games. No evidence of professional hockey background in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Pardubice hockey hotbed, early goaltending specialization, local pro team access, physical talent
evidence_summary: Hašek grew up in Pardubice, a Czech hockey hotbed, and was immersed in the sport from age 6 when his father bought him goalie equipment. He was tall for his age and had a natural goaltending instinct, joining the 9-year-old team at age 5-6. By 16, he was the youngest professional player in Czechoslovak history with HC Pardubice. His working-class family (father a miner) supported his early hockey involvement, and the local hockey culture provided the ecosystem for his development despite Iron Curtain limitations.
starting_point: Born to a working-class family in Pardubice, Czechoslovakia; father was a miner, parents divorced when he was 2; stepfather Jan Hašek adopted him and supported his early hockey involvement.
current_position: Retired NHL legend and Hockey Hall of Famer; active in Czech politics, ran for Czech Senate in 2024; vocal critic of Russia's invasion of Ukraine; turned 60 in January 2025.

He started playing as a small boy, was the fourth-ranked Belgian player at 13, joined the national team at 13, and became Belgian champion at 15 in 1985.

name: Jacob Bekenstein
milestone_by_age_26: Published his groundbreaking PhD thesis in 1972 at age 25 proposing that black holes have entropy proportional to their event horizon area, launching the field of black hole thermodynamics.
early_history_summary: Bekenstein was born in Mexico City to Polish Jewish immigrants and moved to the US in the early 1960s. He earned his undergraduate and master's degrees from the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn in 1969, then pursued his PhD at Princeton under John Wheeler. By 1972, at age 25, he had published three influential papers on black hole thermodynamics, including his groundbreaking proposal that black holes have entropy.
family_context_summary: Born in Mexico City to Joseph and Esther Bekenstein, Polish Jews who immigrated to Mexico. The family moved to the US in the early 1960s, first to Texas and then to New York. He gained US citizenship in 1968.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of parental scientific or academic background; parents were Polish Jewish immigrants to Mexico.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Princeton, John Wheeler, black hole physics golden age, immigrant drive
evidence_summary: Jacob Bekenstein was born to Polish Jewish immigrants in Mexico City and moved to the US as a teenager. He earned his undergraduate and master's degrees simultaneously from the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn in 1969, then moved to Princeton for his PhD under John Wheeler, one of the leading figures in gravitational physics. At Princeton during the golden age of black hole research (1969-1972), Bekenstein made his groundbreaking proposal that black holes have entropy proportional to their horizon area. His immigrant background and family's move to the US provided access to elite academic institutions.
starting_point: Born in Mexico City to Polish Jewish immigrant parents; family moved to the US in the early 1960s, first to Texas then New York, enabling access to American universities.
current_position: Died on August 16, 2015, at age 68 in Helsinki, Finland, while visiting to present a seminar; was professor emeritus of theoretical physics at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
